title: A simple (inductive) proof for the non-existence of 2-cycles of the 3x+1 problem
status: NOT CONSULTED; the 3x-1 statement below is quoted from Lagarias's annotated bibliography II, entry 95, attested and not observed
notes: J. Number Theory 123 (2007), 10-17, per Lagarias. Registered 20 September 2026 during the search for a published 3x-1 verification floor. Per Lagarias's entry 95, the paper gives a second proof that the 3x+1 function has no nontrivial 2-cycles on the positive integers, and its last section sketches a proof that the 3x-1 function on the positive integers has a single 2-cycle, with minimal element 17 -- equivalently, the 3x+1 function on the negative integers has a single 2-cycle, at -17. The method applies to 3x +- q with gcd(6, q) = 1 to give a finite list of 2-cycles, and does not extend to m >= 3; for that see Simons and de Weger (2005) and simons-2008-m-cycles-generalized-syracuse. WHY IT MATTERS HERE. It is the only theorem-type m-cycle statement on the negative side that the search found: a result of the Steiner / Simons-de Weger kind for 3x-1, which is what no verification floor supplies (docs/problems/juggler_negative_floor_3x1.md). Read it before the next cycle branch claims anything about negative m-cycles; a DOI is deliberately not recorded until the paper is seen.
